title: "Recreating the beautiful graph"

## Background

The chemicals k_mgl, mg_mgl, no3, Ca,     NH4 are stream polutants and negatively impact the health of aquatic environments. After a hurricane affected Puerto Rico there was concern that stream polutants had increased in concentration, and this analysis ponders that hypothesis.

But mostly, we are tasked with recreating this graph

![This is the inspo](https://eds-214-reproducibility-m26.github.io/course-materials/interactive/images/Schaefer_etal_2020_fig3.png)

## Data


Data was pulled from the [McDowell and International Institute Of Tropical Foresty](https://eds-214-reproducibility-m26.github.io/course-materials/interactive/interactive-day1am.html#ref-mcdowell2024
). Four sets of data were used for this analysis, coming from four streams: QuebradaCuenca1, QuebradaCuenca2, QuebradaCuenca3, and RioMameyesPuente. 

## Methods

Concentrations of k_mgl, mg_mgl, no3, Ca, NH4 were analysed in 9 week moving averages.


## Results
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
values <- read_csv("../output/cleandata.csv")

values |>
  ggplot(
    mapping = aes(x = window_start, y = conc, color = site)
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(vars(Chem), scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = dmy("1-12-1989"))
```

The above graph demonstrates how concentrations changed after the hurricane event (illustrated by the vertical line occuring in 1989). It looks like there is a small, but lasting increase in concentrations following the hurricane. And more importantly, it kinda looks like the inspo graph.
